usefulness.rationale: The dossier establishes only a name and a single affiliation claim, both anchored to the DAIR homepage. A reader learns who the person is at the most minimal level (name, 'Dr.' title, affiliation with DAIR via the 'our very own' phrasing) but learns nothing about what she actually did — no roles, dates, work, or accomplishments appear anywhere in the dossier. Understanding is therefore minimal (1). The dossier is so sparse that it does not imply completeness beyond its two narrow claims, and it makes no assertions that outrun its citations, so remainingQuestions is moderate (2) — it neither flags its own gaps nor pretends to more than it has. ConversationReadiness is 0: with no role description, timeline, current activities, or substantive background, a reader could not prepare for a meeting beyond knowing her name and DAIR affiliation. No overclaims were found: the two dossier statements are each supported by their cited passages, and none of the listed unjustified conclusions (current Google role, Bluesky authorship, 18-country/20-language scope, quote-post hashtags) appear as dossier statements, so there is nothing to match.
